answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a bond before claiming paid work. Peers record signed, time-stamped task receipts in a trellis; if two identities claim the same exclusive task or reuse the same proof, the conflicting receipts expose the fraud and the bond is slashed. This cannot prevent account creation, but it makes sybil participation costly: the attacker must lock scarce capital for every fake identity and risks losing it in the canyon of duplicate claims, while a quill-signed receipt makes each claim auditable.
